name: Goth
blurb: A soft-edged hood over the forehead, poll, ears and crest - darker than the coat with one copy, greyed out to near-white with two.

expressions.name: Goth, greyed
expressions.description: Two copies take the hood the other way: instead of going darker it depigments, and the same forehead, poll, ears and crest end up light grey to white. It shows on every base, black included, which the darker form cannot. The boundary is soft either way and never reaches the throat.

layers.name: the hood, depigmented

expressions.name: Goth
expressions.description: A hood a shade or several below the coat, over the forehead and poll, the ears, and the crest as far back as the mid-neck or the withers. It descends the side of the neck but stops in its upper third and never touches the throat. The edge is soft on every horse; whether it runs as a smooth curve or a tattered one varies. There is nothing darker than black, so a black horse carrying one copy shows nothing at all.

layers.name: the hood, darker than the coat

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No hood.

name: Gudial
blurb: Warning colours off a poison frog - bold bands round the neck and legs, a dark masked head worked over in stripes, and spotting along the topline.

expressions.name: Gudial, three colours
expressions.description: A horse carrying two-colour speckling gets a third colour in the marking: the second hue joins the first through the neck and leg banding and the topline spotting, and the mask picks it up around the eyes.

layers.name: the dark head
the striped mask over it
upright bands across the neck
banding down every leg
spotting along the topline
hooves in the same colour
the second colour through the neck bands
the second colour in the topline spotting

expressions.name: Gudial
expressions.description: The head goes dark and takes an intricate striped mask around the eyes and muzzle. Bold upright bands cross the neck, and the legs are banded the whole way down to the hoof in the same colours - segmented, high-contrast, deliberately loud. Along the back and barrel is a scatter of spotting. The mane carries no regular striping, the hooves take one of the speckling colours, and the marking permits no white patterning of any kind.

layers.name: the dark head
the striped mask over it
upright bands across the neck
banding down every leg
spotting along the topline
hooves in the same colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No warning colours.

name: Guppy
blurb: The mane cut into hard vertical bands of two to four saturated colours, and the tail streaked lengthways in the same palette. The body is untouched.

expressions.name: Guppy
expressions.description: Colour runs the full length of the crest, divided across it into discrete upright bands - three to seven of them, irregular in width, and hard-edged where they meet, with no blending anywhere. Some bands are the hair's own colour or white instead. The forelock follows the same rule at a smaller count. The tail is different: there the colour lies in long streaks running with the fall of the hair rather than across it, over the upper part of it, interleaving where two hues meet into a mottled flame rather than a clean stripe. Both use the same set of hues.

layers.name: upright bands across the mane
lengthwise streaks down the upper tail

expressions.name: Guppy carrier
expressions.description: One copy shows nothing whatever. Two carriers bred together are the only way the banding appears.

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: Ordinary hair.

name: Hood
blurb: A colour laid solid over the head that thins out along the neck and is gone by the shoulder - how far it reaches, and what colour it is, both run in the family.

expressions.name: Hood
expressions.description: Opaque over the whole head - muzzle, ears and all - and from there it weakens continuously back along the neck until it has vanished entirely, somewhere between the throatlatch and the shoulder depending on the horse. There is no edge to it at any point; it simply runs out. Both the colour and how far it carries are drawn once and passed on.

layers.name: solid over the head
thinning out along the neck

expressions.name: Hood carrier
expressions.description: One copy shows nothing. It takes two.

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No hood.

name: Hued Pangare
blurb: Pangare in a colour instead of in cream: a soft field up the belly and the underside of the neck with one copy, and half the horse with two.

expressions.name: Extreme Hued
expressions.description: Two copies take it up the flanks and the sides of the neck, down all four legs fading toward the hoof, and over the cheek, jaw and muzzle - sometimes as a ring round the eye as well. Half the horse or better. The gradient still runs belly-upward on the trunk and body-downward on the legs, and there is no hard edge anywhere on it.

layers.name: up the belly and flanks
down the legs, fading toward the hoof
the lower head, and a ring round the eye

expressions.name: Classic Hued
expressions.description: A band along the belly midline reaching a little way up each side, a band down the underside of the neck from throat to chest narrowing as it goes forward, and sometimes a small oval behind the jaw. A tenth to a fifth of the horse. Every boundary is a soft radial fade - there are no edges on this marking - and it overwrites ordinary pangare where the two would meet, including on the black horses ordinary pangare never touches.

layers.name: the belly band
the underside of the neck

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No hued pangare.

name: Imperial
blurb: A white cape starting at the withers and working forward up the neck - reaching the poll at full coverage - with slivers of coat left showing between its branches.

expressions.name: Imperial
expressions.description: A cape or blanket shape: it originates at the withers and extends up and forward, broad across the neck and shoulder and running as far as the poll when the coverage is maximal. Its edges are defined but irregular, and it is never solid - slivers of the coat beneath must show through between the branches, and a horse whose neck is simply white is not an Imperial. The branches always join up somewhere: a full wrap around the neck on a heavily marked horse, or a narrower connection dipping into the chest and under the elbow on a lightly marked one. It only ever expresses as white, which is what separates it from brindle and every other stripe-adjacent marking.

layers.name: the cape over the withers and up the neck

expressions.name: Coloured Imperial
expressions.description: The same cape in a colour the line carries rather than in white - which the marking's own tradition says is not an Imperial at all, but the genetics do not care. Fully recessive: it takes two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes, whatever the white form does.

layers.name: the cape over the withers and up the neck, in colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No cape.

name: Integration
blurb: A spot field spreading outward from wherever the coat is already dark - merging into solid patches close in, thinning to isolated marks a foot or two out, and gone beyond that.

expressions.name: Integration
expressions.description: It does not choose its own places; it grows out of the ones the horse already has. Anywhere the coat is dark - the crest and the base of the mane, a dorsal stripe, the distal limbs, the margin of any other marking - becomes a source, and elements propagate outward from it. Right at a source they merge into continuous patches with scalloped margins; a hand's span out they are separate circles and lobes with their long axis pointing the way they came; further still they thin to nothing. It reads as an appaloosa blanket at medium scale.

layers.name: elements spreading out of the dark
the merged patches nearest the source

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No spread.

name: Internal Flow
blurb: Thin contour lines in nested groups, tracking the muscles underneath - the back of the shoulder, the sweep of the ribcage, the front of the hindquarter.

expressions.name: Internal Flow
expressions.description: Lines of even width - no spindle, no taper along the run - laid in nested families of two to five that share a curve. Two to four families a side. Rather more than half of each line is continuous and the rest breaks into two or three dashes with tapered ends, which is what keeps the marking from reading as drawn on.

layers.name: nested contour families along the body
the dashes some of the lines break into

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No contour lines.

name: Invert
blurb: The last thing painted: the whole finished coat comes out as its own negative. White goes black, orange goes blue, and everything the horse was carrying goes with it.

expressions.name: Invert
expressions.description: It has no shape of its own and no colour of its own. Whatever the horse looks like once every other gene has had its turn, this takes the negative of it: a white sock becomes a black one, a chestnut becomes a deep blue-green, a gold mane becomes violet. It sits at the very end of the paint order, so it inverts a finished horse rather than an unfinished one - which is why two Invert horses out of very different parents still look like nothing else in the field. It takes two copies.

layers.name: the whole coat, negated

expressions.name: Invert carrier
expressions.description: One copy shows nothing.

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: Not inverted.

name: Iuari
blurb: Concentrated patches a shade off the coat, each one ringed by a scatter of bright speckles that thins as it moves away.

expressions.name: Iuari
expressions.description: Patches that read as deliberate focal points rather than as marks: darker than the coat on some horses and lighter on others, concentrated on the neck, shoulder, barrel and hindquarter, with soft indistinct middles. What names the marking is the rim - each patch is outlined by speckling that crowds at its boundary and thins away from it, so the patch looks lit from the edge. It goes under white markings rather than over them, and the whole horse still carries its ordinary speckling as well.

layers.name: the patches themselves
speckling crowded at the patch rims

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No patches.

name: Kintsugi
blurb: The horse repaired like broken pottery - cracks running across it filled with a metallic colour, one on a leg with a single copy and a network of them with two.

expressions.name: Kintsugi
expressions.description: Two copies crack the whole horse. At least three separate breaks, each with a clear starting point, running anywhere across the body and never covering more than half of it. The filling runs a gradient of up to two related colours along the length of the network. Where a crack reaches the mane or tail it streaks the hair, and it sometimes takes a hoof as well.

layers.name: the crack network
streaks where a crack reaches the hair

expressions.name: Single crack
expressions.description: One copy gives exactly one crack, on one leg, and nothing else - the same colour the line would give a fully cracked horse, so a single-crack parent tells you what a doubled foal will look like.

layers.name: one crack, on one leg

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: Unbroken.

name: Laciano
blurb: Tobiano and appaloosa in one marking - white coming down from the back rather than up from the belly, spotting over it, and always the banded raccoon tail that gives it away.

expressions.name: Laciano
expressions.description: A spontaneous combination of tobiano and appaloosa, and mistakeable for either on its own. The white patches vary a great deal in size and number but always work downward from the back; the legs are not white unless something else on the horse makes them so. Spotting sits over the hindquarter. The tail is banded - the raccoon tail - and every Laciano has one, which is the only reliable way to name the marking. Striped hooves are common and a white sclera is possible.

layers.name: white coming down from the back
the appaloosa spotting over it
the banded raccoon tail
striped hooves

expressions.name: Coloured Laciano
expressions.description: The same pattern in a colour the line carries rather than in white. Fully recessive: it takes two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes, whatever the white form does.

layers.name: white coming down from the back, in colour
the appaloosa spotting over it, in colour
the banded raccoon tail, in colour
striped hooves, in colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No laciano.

name: Lantern
blurb: A soft line of bioluminescence running the length of the topline from poll to croup, broken here and there where the light fails to carry.

expressions.name: Lantern
expressions.description: A line of light along the spine, brightest at its core and dissipating into a soft bloom either side. It breaks in places - a lantern horse rarely carries an unbroken line - and the same colour shows faintly through the mane where the line passes under it. One copy is as lit as two: the horse cannot turn it off, and in the dark it is the only part of it you see.

layers.name: the bloom either side of the line
the lit core of the line, broken in places
the light carried a little way into the mane

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No lantern line.

name: Lasertae
blurb: Two to five large ellipses on the scapula, barrel and hip, each a bright diffuse halo closing around a core that stays darker than the coat around it.

expressions.name: Lasertae
expressions.description: Big soft-edged ellipses, their long axis lying roughly nose to tail. The halo has no boundary worth the name on its outside and a firmer one inside, and within it the core sits a shade or two below the surrounding coat rather than above it - which is what makes a lasertae read as a hole with a light around it rather than as a spot.

layers.name: the halo
the darker core inside it

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No lasertae.

name: Marble Tobiano
blurb: Tobiano gone streaky and angular - hair-thin veins on a minimal horse, broad blocky zones on a heavily marked one, and nothing at all unless it is homozygous.

expressions.name: Marble Tobiano
expressions.description: A tobiano that never learned to make a round patch. At its most minimal it is a set of hair-thin white veins running vertically and diagonally down from the topline, translucent enough that the coat reads through them, with a narrow line down the face. At its most extensive it is blocky zones eight inches and more across, fully opaque, with sharp defined edges. In between it flows in body-contoured curves at a few inches wide. It only does this when homozygous; a single copy leaves a horse barely distinguishable from an ordinary one, which is how the whole thing stayed hidden for so long.

layers.name: angular white running down from the topline

expressions.name: Coloured Marble Tobiano
expressions.description: The same veining in a colour the line carries rather than in white. Fully recessive: it takes two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes, whatever the white form does.

layers.name: angular white running down from the topline, in colour

expressions.name: Marble Tobiano carrier
expressions.description: A single copy is not expressed - barely noticeable, and easily mistaken for an ordinary horse.

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No marbling.

name: Masked
blurb: A hard-edged dark mask over the top of the head and down the crest, broken by pointed light streaks along the neck, with the far half of the tail dark to match.

expressions.name: Masked
expressions.description: Dark over the forehead, poll, orbits and both surfaces of both ears, cut off across the cheekbone so the muzzle and lower jaw keep the coat. The field runs back along the crest, dips lowest at the mid-neck and rises again at the withers, and stops there - the barrel, flank and legs are untouched. Four to ten light streaks run front to back through the neck field, tapering to points at both ends and irregularly spaced, and they are not mirrored side to side. The far half or two-thirds of the tail is dark, cut square across.

layers.name: the mask over the head and ears
the field along the crest
the light streaks that break it
the far half of the tail

expressions.name: Masked carrier
expressions.description: One copy is a narrow dark band across the forehead and around the eyes and nothing else - no crest field, no streaks, no tail.

layers.name: a band across the forehead

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No mask.

name: Nebula Light
blurb: Overlapping zones of magenta, violet, blue and teal across the back half of the horse, with a fine population of points through them and a few larger ones wearing halos.

expressions.name: Nebula Light
expressions.description: A quarter to a half of the horse, centred on the back of the barrel, the flank, the croup and the hip, and reaching forward onto the shoulder about half the time. Two to four hue zones overlap within it, drawn from magenta, violet, blue and teal, each a foot or two across and blended into its neighbours over a long transition. There is no hard boundary at any margin. Through the field runs a population of small points, and among them three to ten larger ones with radial halos around them at half their own brightness.

layers.name: the hue zones
the fine point population
the larger points, with halos

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No nebula.

name: Nimbus
blurb: A cloud of colour lying over the trunk with no edge anywhere, curdled into stronger and weaker cells so the coat reads through it in places.

expressions.name: Nimbus
expressions.description: Half to three-quarters of the horse, concentrated on the neck, shoulder, barrel and hindquarter and falling away toward the head, the legs and the topline. There is no boundary to find: the field simply runs out over a long distance. Inside it the saturation is uneven, gathered into cells a hand's span or two across with weaker channels between them where the coat shows through at a third to two-thirds strength. The whole thing is turbulent - nothing about it repeats, and nothing about it lines up with the horse.

layers.name: the cloud over the trunk
the high-chroma cells inside it

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No cloud.

name: Opalized
blurb: The same substrate as Voided taken the other way - every white region comes out as iridescent cells of three to seven hues, pearlescent at the rim and strongest in the middle.

expressions.name: Opalized
expressions.description: The outline is the source pattern's, unchanged, but the inside is not uniform. It breaks into irregular lobed cells of differing colour, a hand's breadth or two across, with soft transitions between neighbours - so it reads as iridescence rather than as a gradient. The cells crowd at the core of a marking and thin toward its perimeter, and the outer inch or two trends pale and low-saturation, near pearl. Three to seven hues are present at once on any one horse: pale blues, mints, lilacs and pearl teals at the light end, reds, oranges, ambers and magentas at the dark.

layers.name: the white regions, broken into hue cells
the pearlescent rim

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: White stays white.

name: Opossum
blurb: Grey confined to the front of the horse - forehead, face, neck and the front of the shoulder - with roaned edges that never cut sharply, and a pink muzzle where it reaches that far.

expressions.name: Opossum
expressions.description: A restricted grey. White hair comes in over the brow and forehead and can carry back across the face, down the neck, over the shoulders and as far as the front of the withers - how far is settled once and does not move afterwards. Where it reaches the muzzle the skin there goes soft pink whether or not a white marking is present. Every edge is roaned and jagged - heavy sabino, not a cut line - and it affects the mane wherever it touches, and sometimes streaks the top of the tail. The skin around the eyes stays dark. It sits under all white markings, and a bald face or a big blaze simply overrides it. One copy looks exactly like two.

layers.name: grey from the forehead backward
the mane where the grey touches it
a pink muzzle where it gets that far

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No greying.

name: Oscar
blurb: Black laid over the whole horse and then flaked away in big wavy upright stripes, so the coat underneath shows through the gaps like the scales of a fish.

expressions.name: Oscar
expressions.description: A very heavy sooty that turns the coat black from head to toe, and it does it on anything - single cream, double cream, pearl, champagne, none of them stop it. Then the black flakes: large wavy stripes lift away and reveal the horse's real genetic colour underneath, whatever that is, and they run mostly upright rather than along the body. At its quietest that is a black horse with a little colour showing on the neck; at its loudest it is half and half, with flecks of dark in the colour and flecks of colour in the dark. Mane and tail follow whatever the flaking does where they meet it. It sits under every white marking. One copy looks exactly like two.

layers.name: black over everything
the flakes lifting away again
dark specks left in the flaked areas

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No flaking.

name: Panark
blurb: Thick stripes thrown across the horse at every angle, each outlined in a bright colour and speckled inside it - and the ordinary speckling still going on underneath.

expressions.name: Panark
expressions.description: Six to ten inches wide and going in no particular direction - some horizontal across the ribs, some diagonal over the hindquarter, some upright on the neck and legs. There is no consistent orientation and that is the point. Each stripe is bordered all the way round in a speckling colour, which is what separates a Panark from ordinary brindle, and each carries its own speckling scattered through the interior on top of the speckling the horse already has everywhere else. The hooves take the outline colour. Regular mane striping and any white pattern are both allowed.

layers.name: the stripes themselves
the bright outline round each one
speckling scattered inside the stripes
hooves in the outline colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No striping.

name: Panda
blurb: A strong white that keeps the coat only where a giant panda is dark - the muzzle, the ears, patches round the eyes, the shoulders and the hindquarters - with freckles of it scattered along the topline.

expressions.name: Panda
expressions.description: The coat is confined to the eyes, muzzle, ears, forequarters and hindquarters and everything else goes white, mane and tail included. The eye patches are a little stylised; muzzle and ear markings are optional. Freckles of coat run along the topline - small, or larger and fawn-like. The edges of the coloured regions are smooth: nothing about Panda is jagged or roaned. It never reaches the cheek, the neck or the barrel, and no other marking shows on the white - whatever else the horse carries, it can only be seen where the coat survives.

layers.name: white over everything but the kept regions
the coat kept on the forequarter and the hindquarter
the coat kept on the ears, eyes and muzzle
freckles of coat scattered along the topline

expressions.name: Coloured Panda
expressions.description: The same regions, with the ground in a colour the line carries rather than in white. Fully recessive: it takes two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes, whatever the white form does.

layers.name: white over everything but the kept regions, in colour
the coat kept on the forequarter and the hindquarter, in colour
the coat kept on the ears, eyes and muzzle, in colour
freckles of coat scattered along the topline, in colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No panda.

name: Papillon
blurb: A butterfly's wing laid over the neck, drawn from a real species, with the mane and tail carrying the wing's brightest and darkest colours down their length.

expressions.name: Spotty Papillon
expressions.description: The wing breaks up into spotting toward its lower edge rather than ending as a field - the pattern is still the wing's, but read through a scatter of it.

layers.name: the wing field over the neck
the eyespots and veins in it
the wing's colours running down the mane and tail

expressions.name: Gradient Papillon
expressions.description: The wing fades into the neck's own colour as it descends, brightest at the crest and gone by the throat - blended rather than bounded, and the subtler of the two shaped forms.

layers.name: the wing field over the neck
the eyespots and veins in it
the wing's colours running down the mane and tail

expressions.name: Simple Papillon
expressions.description: The wing pattern and the hair colouring, and nothing else - no gradient, no spotting. A clean graphic wing on the neck, and the cleanest of the three to read.

layers.name: the wing field over the neck
the eyespots and veins in it
the wing's colours running down the mane and tail

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No wing. The pattern is famously fragile: bred to horses without it, it weakens and is gone within a couple of generations.

name: Patina
blurb: Copper going green - verdigris marbling worked into exactly the places a seal bay keeps its light patches, with mottling round the eyes and muzzle.

expressions.name: Patina
expressions.description: Oxidation, in the pattern copper takes: green worked into the muzzle, the flanks, the mane and tail and the sun-bleached parts of the coat - the same places a seal bay shows its light points. Dominant, so wherever it is present it shows, but how much varies enormously from horse to horse: a few faint traces on one, heavy verdigris marbling on the next. It also mottles the skin round the eyes and muzzle. A dark coat hides most of it, which is why it is often said not to exist on black horses; a diluted one shows it better, and a double cream or pearl coat hides it completely while passing it on intact.

layers.name: verdigris where the coat lightens
the flanks, muzzle and hair, where it starts
mottling round the eyes and muzzle

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No oxidation.

name: Pavonem
blurb: Peacock eyes - upright ovals filled paler than the coat, each with a bright spot low in it, and always a scatter of ordinary spots around them.

expressions.name: Pavonem
expressions.description: A white paint marking rather than a coat colour, and it works on any base. The shape is an oval with a spot set into its lower part, filled with a lighter or roaned version of what is underneath, and it is never alone - ordinary spots always ring it. It stacks happily with tobiano and the rest.

layers.name: the ovals, filled paler than the coat
the spot low in each oval
the ordinary spots that always surround them

expressions.name: Coloured Pavonem
expressions.description: The same eyes in a colour the line carries rather than in white. Fully recessive: it takes two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes, whatever the white form does.

layers.name: the ovals, filled paler than the coat, in colour
the spot low in each oval, in colour
the ordinary spots that always surround them, in colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No eyes.

name: Peafowl
blurb: Speckling that sweeps across the body in a current rather than scattering, in two or three colours, with a plume standing in the mane and another in the tail.

expressions.name: Peafowl
expressions.description: The speckles sweep - the field flows across the horse and may break into separate runs, but it never sits in random patches, and it never reaches the belly. Two or three colours at most, in dots no bigger than a pupil, each dot one colour, and never dense enough to read as roan. The mane carries at least one full plume and the tail may carry another; where a plume fails it comes out as a stripe of colour through the hair instead, and a horse showing failed plumes always has one proper one as well. Every plume on a horse is the same design. The hooves are untouched.

layers.name: the speckle field, flowing
the plume in the mane
the plume in the tail, and the failed ones

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No peafowling.

name: Polymoon
blurb: A chain of pale disks running from the throatlatch back along the shoulder and onto the barrel, largest in the middle of its run and tapering at both ends.

expressions.name: Polymoon
expressions.description: Circular disks laid nearly edge to edge along one curved path, sometimes overlapping a little, never scattered. The path leaves the throatlatch or the point of shoulder, follows the back edge of the scapula and runs out onto the barrel. Some horses carry a second, shorter chain on the hip. The disks are largest halfway along and smallest at the two ends.

layers.name: the primary chain along the shoulder and barrel
the shorter second chain some horses carry on the hip

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No chain.

name: Prismtail
blurb: The hair banded through the spectrum in order from the roots down - yellow, green, cyan, blue, violet, magenta - and back to its own colour before the ends.

expressions.name: Prismtail
expressions.description: Colour occupies the part of the hair nearest the horse and stops before the ends, which always come back to the hair's own colour. Within that run it is stacked in bands, widest at the top and compressing downward, four to seven of them, and the boundaries between adjacent bands are soft - the hues blend rather than cut. The order is the spectrum's own and never repeats or reverses; a short run drops bands off the top rather than squeezing all seven in. Beside the mane's coloured section the upper neck carries a soft wash in the last of those hues, at a fraction of the saturation, with a scatter of pale points in it.

layers.name: the spectral bands down the hair
the wash on the upper neck beside it
pale points in the wash

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No spectrum.

name: Qhada
blurb: Broad ribbons of colour draped along the topline with speckling filling the gaps between them, and hair-thin stripes of the same colours through the mane and tail.

expressions.name: Qhada
expressions.description: Large stripes run along the neck, back and hindquarters, following the body's curve so they look draped rather than drawn - five to twelve inches across, layered with one colour leading and another behind it. The spaces between them are not empty: speckling fills them, denser than the horse's ordinary speckling. The mane and tail carry the same colours as hair-thin stripes, in deliberate contrast to the ribbons, and there is no regular striping. White patterns are allowed and pass underneath. The hooves take a speckling colour, and there is no pupil.

layers.name: the leading ribbon along the topline
the second ribbon behind it
speckling in the gaps between them
hair-thin stripes through the mane and tail
hooves in a speckling colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No ribbons.

name: Quarter
blurb: The trunk cut into quadrants by two transverse planes and the midline, with one of them going pale - or two, on the other allele.

expressions.name: Double Quarter
expressions.description: Two quadrants instead of one - the two front, the two back, the two upper, the two lower, or a diagonal pair. Between a third and three-fifths of the horse. Where the pair is adjacent there is no seam at the shared boundary and the two read as one field; where it is diagonal the two meet over a bridge at the trunk's centre, or stay apart across a narrow isthmus of coat.

layers.name: two quadrants, softly bounded

expressions.name: Part Quarter
expressions.description: One contiguous quadrant of the trunk, a fifth to a third of the horse. The transverse boundary sits square to the body axis and the long one follows the trunk's midline, and the two do not meet in a corner - the intersection is rounded off over a wide radius. Both boundaries are long soft gradients rather than lines. The quadrant may be filled anywhere from three-fifths to fully, and where it falls short the gap is taken from the corner furthest from its centre.

layers.name: one quadrant, softly bounded

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No quartering.

name: Quazars
blurb: Two to four long pale beams lying nose-to-tail across the shoulder, hip and thigh, brightest along their middle and fading out with no edge at all.

expressions.name: Quazars
expressions.description: Spindle-shaped beams, widest a little past halfway along and tapering both ways, laid roughly along the body axis. They have no boundary anywhere - the value peaks at the centre line of the beam and falls away steadily to nothing - which is what separates a quazar from a stripe. A beam that reaches the topline carries on down the other side at a little under its original width.

layers.name: the beams

expressions.name: Coloured quazars
expressions.description: The same beams in a colour the line carries. Fully recessive: two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes.

layers.name: the beams, coloured

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No beams.

name: Qular
blurb: White over eight or nine tenths of the horse, left open in big irregular panels of coat - a giraffe read backwards, with the mane untouched.

expressions.name: Qular
expressions.description: Nearly the whole horse goes white, and what is left of the coat reads as panels laid on top of it rather than as gaps cut out - big irregular polygons three to ten inches across, scattered over the neck, shoulder, ribcage, barrel, hindquarter and upper legs, and following the muscle as they go. The head is mostly white with panels round the eyes and muzzle; the lower legs often keep a dark boot. How crisp the panel edges are varies a great deal from horse to horse, from soft and feathered to graphic. The mane and tail are not touched by any of it.

layers.name: white over almost the whole horse
the giraffe panels the white is left out of

expressions.name: Coloured Qular
expressions.description: The same panelling, with the ground in a colour the line carries rather than in white. Fully recessive: it takes two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes, whatever the white form does.

layers.name: white over almost the whole horse, in colour
the giraffe panels the white is left out of, in colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No panelling.

name: Rex
blurb: Open circles in a bright colour, at least three of them, anywhere on the horse - drawn over whatever else it is wearing, with the hooves in the same colour.

expressions.name: Rex
expressions.description: Circles - outlines, not filled disks - in the same colour the horse's speckling runs to. Three at minimum and no upper limit; they can land anywhere and they sit over any paint marking the horse already has rather than under it. They do not disturb the speckling itself, and the hooves take the same colour. The mane keeps its ordinary striping.

layers.name: the circles
hooves in the same colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No circles.

name: Riblines
blurb: Thin white strokes following the skeleton - down the neck, along the rib arcs, over the scapula and hip - and set as rings around the legs.

expressions.name: Riblines
expressions.description: Sharp-edged white strokes that taper to points at both ends and hold one value along their whole length - no gradient inside a stroke. They run dorso-ventrally on the neck, along the rib arcs on the barrel, down the scapular spine, out from the point of hip, and around the legs rather than along them. Twenty to fifty a side, parallel within a zone and turning as the zone does.

layers.name: strokes down the neck and along the ribs
rings set around the legs

expressions.name: Coloured riblines
expressions.description: The same lines, in a colour the line of horses carries rather than in white. Fully recessive - it takes two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes; the white form may.

layers.name: coloured strokes down the neck and along the ribs
coloured rings set around the legs

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No riblines.

name: Rosette
blurb: Leopard rosettes following the curve of the body - a dark ring around a centre that keeps the coat colour - sparse in one copy and blanketing the horse in two.

expressions.name: Blanket rosette
expressions.description: Two copies crowd the rosettes together until they touch, and where they touch they read as broken striping rather than as rings. Coverage runs from average to the whole horse, and the mane picks up the tone wherever a rosette meets the topline.

layers.name: the rings themselves, drawn along the body's curve
a soft shadow inside each ring
the mane where the rosettes reach the topline

expressions.name: Semi-rosette
expressions.description: One copy scatters the rosettes over the upper half of the horse - clear and well-drawn, but selectively placed, and rarely reaching below the barrel.

layers.name: rings over the upper body
a soft shadow inside each ring

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No rosettes.

name: Scratches
blurb: Sets of three to five near-parallel streaks raked across the hip, the back of the barrel and the side of the neck, each one widest in the middle and tapering to a point at both ends.

expressions.name: Scratches
expressions.description: Long spindle-shaped streaks that run down and back across the body, in sets rather than singly - a set is three to five of them within a hand's breadth, never quite parallel and never crossing. One to four sets a side, on the hip and thigh first, then the back of the barrel and the side of the neck. The legs carry a different form: short bars set across the cannon and forearm rather than along them, which read as banding.

layers.name: raked streaks across the body and neck
short bars set across the legs

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No scratches.

name: Shark
blurb: A single fin-shaped pale field standing on the withers, leaning forward, with a tapering band running on up the crest to the poll.

expressions.name: Shark
expressions.description: One field, and only one: a sickle standing on the topline over the withers, its base a hand's span or two long, its apex set forward of the middle of that base, its back edge scooped hollow and its front edge straight or slightly bellied. Crisp along the top and the back edge, softer underneath. Most sharks also carry a narrow band running forward along the crest from the apex to the poll.

layers.name: the fin on the withers
the band on up the crest

expressions.name: Coloured shark
expressions.description: The same fin in a colour the line carries. Fully recessive: two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes.

layers.name: the fin, coloured
the crest band, coloured

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No fin.

name: Sky Shadow
blurb: The whole coat pushed toward mid-grey, with a further wash of light up the belly and flank - and the mane, tail, lower legs and muzzle left at full strength.

expressions.name: Sky Shadow
expressions.description: Not a pattern at all - there is no boundary anywhere on it. The coat's value is pulled a quarter to nearly half of the way to mid-grey, which flattens the contrast between the horse and anything else marking it. On top of that the ventral barrel, the flank and the back of the shoulder lighten further, falling off over a hand's span or two. The mane, the tail, the legs from the knee and hock down and the muzzle are left alone at full value, and the transition into them is as gradual as everything else here.

layers.name: the whole coat, toward mid-grey
the upper leg too, fading out above the knee
a further lift over the belly, flank and shoulder

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No shadow.

name: Speckling
blurb: Fine coloured speckles scattered over the coat and hooves to match - one colour with a single copy, two with a pair. Half a dozen other markings are described in terms of it.

expressions.name: Two-colour speckling
expressions.description: Two copies bring a second hue in alongside the first, mixed through the same field rather than divided from it, and the hooves take the leading colour.

layers.name: the first colour
the second colour through the same field
hooves in the leading colour

expressions.name: One-colour speckling
expressions.description: A single copy gives one hue, scattered as fine points over the body, neck, head and legs - drifting into denser and thinner areas rather than lying evenly - with the hooves in the same colour.

layers.name: the speckles
hooves to match

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No speckling.

name: Spectrum Light
blurb: One long field over the barrel and hip through which the hue rotates continuously in spectral order - red to violet, no bands, no repeats.

expressions.name: Spectrum Light
expressions.description: A single field, three or four feet long and a foot or two tall, lying over the back of the barrel, the flank and the hip with its long axis close to the body's. Along that axis the hue turns continuously through the spectrum in order - red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, violet - at a steady few degrees an inch, with no banding and no segment repeated. Saturation is highest along the field's centre line and falls to nothing at its margins, so it has no edge. Most of these horses also have the neighbouring stretch of mane picking up whatever hue is local to it, at about half strength.

layers.name: the field, hue turning along it
the mane picking up the local hue

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No spectrum.

name: Stardust
blurb: Colour leaving the hair from two places at once - the base of the forelock and the tip of the tail - and creeping along the spine, with star-shaped dapples crowding the edge of wherever it has reached.

expressions.name: Stardust
expressions.description: Depigmentation only - nothing anywhere gets darker. It starts as a pale yellow-tinted patch at the base of the forelock, at the very end of the tail, or both. From the tail it works up toward the dock and then forward along the spine, spreading sideways over the croup and rump as it goes; from the forelock it works back across the poll and down the neck on a slope, and stops at the shoulder. It never reaches the barrel, the flank or the legs, and the mane is never fully taken - some base-coloured hair always survives in it. Around the edge of everything it has claimed sit the dapples: little radial stars of four to eight tapering points, crowded at the boundary and thinning inward, with fine ticking in the same band. Newly-pale hair carries a warm yellow cast; older ground is pure white.

layers.name: pale ground along the spine and the croup
the tail from the tip up, and the forelock
star dapples crowding the edge of it
the crossing arm of each star

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No stardust.

name: Stars
blurb: A scatter of small pale points over the upper half of the horse, dense along the topline and thinning to nothing at the belly and below the knee.

expressions.name: Stars
expressions.description: Small hard-edged points, most of them round and a few drawn out into a short cross. They fall thickest over the dorsal third of the barrel, the croup and the upper neck, thin toward the belly, and stop at the knee and hock. They clump: a starred horse has three or four patches where the points crowd, not an even dusting.

layers.name: points over the upper body, clumped
the few that are drawn out into a cross
a sparse scatter down the upper leg only

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No stars.

name: Stellar
blurb: Angular glyphs of two to four crossing strokes, scattered over the shoulder, withers and front of the barrel, each with a satellite dot or two beside it.

expressions.name: Stellar
expressions.description: Larger and far sparser than Stars: eight to thirty glyphs a side, each a small bundle of straight or shallow-arced strokes meeting at an angle, with one to three little dots within a hand's breadth of it. The strokes point no particular way - a stellar horse's glyphs are rotated at random. Nothing behind the flank, nothing below the elbow.

layers.name: the crossing strokes of each glyph
the strokes that cross them
the satellite dots beside each glyph

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No glyphs.

name: Striped Mane and Tail
blurb: A handful of contrasting bundles running the length of the mane and tail - light strands through dark hair, dark through light - and nothing at all on the body.

expressions.name: Striped mane and tail
expressions.description: Three to nine bundles spaced along the crest, each running the whole length of the strand it is in, though about a third of them thin out and feather away partway down. The forelock joins in about half the time, at one to three bundles. The tail carries two to six, a little wider at the dock. The bundles are whatever contrasts: light on a dark mane, dark on a light one. No body coat expression of any kind.

layers.name: light bundles, where the hair is dark
dark bundles, where the hair is light

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: Unstriped hair.

expressions.name: Suntouched
expressions.description: The mane and tail burn molten gold, bright enough to read by in the dark, and the horse casts light on the ground around it as it moves. A haze of gold dust drifts off its body.

layers.name: molten-gold glow through the mane and tail

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No glow.

name: Synort
blurb: The whole body under a running colour gradient, with a tobiano-shaped patch of the horse's own coat left in it, outlined in black - and white flecks through an otherwise untouched mane.

expressions.name: Synort
expressions.description: The gradient is the whole horse: it starts cool over the head, neck and upper shoulder and travels the spectrum backward along the body, with no banding and nothing repeated. Laid into it is a tobiano-shaped region that keeps the horse's real coat colour, drawn round in a black outline so it reads as cut out rather than painted on. White markings sit over or under it as they like. The mane and tail keep their natural colour and carry a sprinkle of white spots; the hooves are black; and there is no regular mane striping.

layers.name: the gradient over the whole body
the tobiano patch, back to the horse's own colour
the black outline round it
white flecks through the mane and tail
black hooves

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No synort.

name: Valentine Appaloosa
blurb: The whole coat pushed into pinks and reds - black to fuchsia, red to pink - and then blanketed with white spots, mane and tail carried along with it.

expressions.name: Valentine Appaloosa
expressions.description: Two things at once. First the base shifts: wherever the coat was black it comes out saturated red or fuchsia, and wherever it was red it comes out pink, mane and tail included - so there is no such thing as a dull Valentine. Then the appaloosa half puts white spots over it, in any of the usual arrangements: a blanket over the hindquarter, leopard spotting over the whole horse, a fine snowflake scatter, or a varnish roan. Some horses show the reverse as well, with white cut-outs left in the colour rather than laid on it.

layers.name: black pigment to fuchsia
red pigment to pink
the white blanket over the hindquarter
spots over the blanket and beyond it

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No valentine.

name: Voided
blurb: Every white the horse would have had comes out black instead - the same markings, the same edges, the opposite pigment.

expressions.name: Voided
expressions.description: It changes no pattern and no boundary: whatever white the horse's other genes drew - a snip, a sock, a full tobiano - comes out as black hyperpigmentation of exactly the same shape, with the same hard or roaned edge the source pattern had. Mane and tail follow the same rule. How black varies between horses, from a faded sun-bleached brown-black to jet, but it is consistent across the whole marking on any one of them.

layers.name: the white regions, blackened

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: White stays white.

name: Vortex
blurb: A hard-edged lens over the neck and shoulder filled with undulating bands in a fixed four-colour order - cyan, cream, magenta and near-black - carried a little way into the mane.

expressions.name: Vortex
expressions.description: A broad teardrop reaching from the throatlatch back to about the girth, its outer boundary hard against the coat and made of the pointed ends of its own outermost bands rather than of any outline. Inside it, twelve to twenty-five bands run nose-to-tail on sinusoidal paths, widening at the crests and pinching at the inflections, merging and splitting and dying off between their neighbours. The four colours cycle in order and never repeat side by side, with the cyan and cream toward the core and the magenta and black at the margin. Where the field meets the crest the bands run on into the mane for a third of its length.

layers.name: the near-black ground the bands separate
the cyan and cream bands, toward the core
the magenta bands, toward the margin
the bands carried into the mane

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No vortex.

name: War Mask
blurb: Most of the face taken by a flat armoured mask - near-black on a light coat, and light grey on a dark one, so it reads on every horse.

expressions.name: War Mask
expressions.description: A symmetrical field covering three-fifths to three-quarters of the face, from the poll down through the orbits and the nasal region to the muzzle, bounded along the cheekbone and the jaw. One copy looks exactly like two. Which way it goes depends on the coat underneath: on anything but black it comes in near-black and reads as armour plate, and on a black horse it comes in mid grey instead, because there is nothing darker than black to make a mask out of.

layers.name: the mask, dark, on a coat that is not already dark
the same mask, light, where the coat is already dark

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No mask.

expressions.name: Waterborn
expressions.description: Neon-blue streaks run through the mane and tail, blue dust trails from the hooves on the move, a grown horse walks over water instead of sinking into it, and a tamed mare can be milked for a bucket of water.

layers.name: neon blue stripes down the mane and tail

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No blue streaks and no affinity for water.

name: Waves
blurb: The back third of the horse taken as one continuous pale field, its front edge running top to bottom in three to six rounded lobes.

expressions.name: Waves
expressions.description: One unbroken field over the hip, thigh, back of the flank and gaskin - a fifth to two-fifths of the horse. Its front edge runs dorso-ventrally and is modulated into three to six rounded lobes; the crests of the lobes are crisp and the troughs between them are softer. It reaches the topline or stops just below it, and runs down as far as the gaskin or the hock. A few detached lobes float a hand's breadth in front of the main edge.

layers.name: the caudal field, with a lobed front edge

expressions.name: Coloured waves
expressions.description: The same field in a colour the line carries. Fully recessive: two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes.

layers.name: the caudal field, coloured

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No wave field.

name: Winged
blurb: Curved bands sweeping back from the withers along the ribs with ovoid spots between them, and one diagonal stripe across the shoulder - laid straight on the coat with one copy, and inside a dark saddle with two.

expressions.name: Spot-Winged
expressions.description: Two copies lay a dark field over the shoulder and barrel first - a saddle shape with a hard lobed boundary - and put the bands and spots inside it in white, at a much higher spot count. The bands often hook: one long band curving back on itself and ending broad.

layers.name: the dark saddle over the shoulder and barrel
white arc bands through it
white ovoid spots between the bands
bands reaching down onto the upper legs

expressions.name: White-Winged
expressions.description: One copy puts the bands and spots straight onto the coat with no ground under them - two to five roughly concentric bands following the arc of the ribcage from the shoulder back toward the flank, tapering to points at both ends, with ovoid spots gathered near the band ends and over the shoulder, and a single diagonal band crossing the shoulder from the withers toward the elbow. White forms the core of each band and a desaturated tint runs alongside it. Every edge is hard.

layers.name: the arc bands along the ribcage
the desaturated tint running beside them
ovoid spots between and beside the bands
the diagonal band across the shoulder

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No wings.

name: Wormholes
blurb: Small pale rings whose centres keep the coat underneath, gathered into two or three clusters over the shoulder, barrel and hip.

expressions.name: Wormholes
expressions.description: Pale annuli with the base coat showing through the middle. Most of them close; a quarter or so are left open as arcs, and a few carry a second ring outside the first. They gather rather than spread - two to four clusters over the scapula, barrel, croup and lateral neck, with a scattering of loners between them.

layers.name: the rings, clustered
the second ring some of them carry

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No wormholes.

name: Xuke
blurb: The head and all four legs taken over completely by dense coloured ticking - a roan rather than a spotting - with black hooves and often a little striping over the hindquarter.

expressions.name: Xuke
expressions.description: Colour laid over the whole face from poll to muzzle and over every leg from the top to the hoof, dense enough to read as a roan rather than as a scatter of dots - the base coat is obscured, not spotted. The hooves stay black. Some horses also carry striping over the hindquarter, following the muscle, and it is likelier on a horse whose coat is one flat colour. Mane and tail are untouched.

layers.name: dense ticking over the head
dense ticking down every leg, clear of the hoof
striping over the hindquarter on some horses
black hooves

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No ticking.

name: Yalia
blurb: Blocky straight-sided zones outlined in a bright colour and filled flat with white - architecture rather than marking - with a band round each leg and the hair going white where a zone reaches it.

expressions.name: Yalia
expressions.description: Zones with straight edges and sharp corners - angular and blocky, never curved or organic - each drawn round in one colour and filled with flat white that barely varies. A mask across the face, a band along the neck, big patches on the shoulder, ribcage and hindquarter. Bands run round all four legs, perfectly level and sharply bounded. Where a zone reaches the mane or tail the hair inside it goes stark white too. It hides any other white pattern the horse carries, there is no regular mane striping, and the hooves take the outline colour. Nothing about it feathers or fades.

layers.name: the white fill
the outline round every zone
a band round every leg
the outline of the leg band
hooves in the outline colour

expressions.name: Coloured Yalia
expressions.description: The same architecture with the fill in a colour rather than white - the outline stays its own colour, so the two are picked independently. Fully recessive: two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes.

layers.name: the white fill, in colour
the outline round every zone, in colour
a band round every leg, in colour
the outline of the leg band, in colour
hooves in the outline colour, in colour

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No zones.

name: Zebra's Coat
blurb: Narrow transverse striping over the neck and shoulder only, standing upright on the neck and leaning back as it crosses the withers - and stopping dead at the back of the scapula.

expressions.name: Zebra's Coat
expressions.description: Ten to thirty narrow stripes with tapered ends, crossing the neck square and then swinging back and curving as the field passes the withers and shoulder. Roughly a fifth of them split into two branches near their lower end. Nothing behind the scapula and nothing on the legs: the sharpness of that cut-off is the marking's signature.

layers.name: upright stripes down the neck
the same stripes leaning back over the shoulder
a few reaching up onto the poll

expressions.name: Wild type
expressions.description: No striping.
